reuse.why: Replaces getDateWithSkippedWeekend with one applyWeekendRule that getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange and the budget template all call; the template wraps it in a small adapter that re-checks skipWeekend.

duplication.why: The weekend/daily/holiday rule exists once; only the occurrence-to-day flatMap is repeated between getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and the template adapter repeats the skipWeekend guard already inside applyWeekendRule.

placement.why: The rule and its holiday predicate live in shared/schedules.ts, handlers stay in server/schedules/app.ts, and rule-utils just carries the new fields into the parsed schedule data.

scope.why: All edits serve the five steps (shared rule, daily skip, range handler, holidays, recurring MM-DD holidays) plus their tests.

maintainability.why: One well-commented rule function with a small typed WeekendRule input; the window sizes (take: 7, count * 7, ±2 days) are magic numbers spread across callers.

disguised_duplication.where: The flatMap(applyWeekendRule -> dayFromDate) repeated in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange is written identically, not disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: applyWeekendRule's WeekendRule input gains frequency and holidays and a daily-skip null branch, all part of the requested rule; server/budget/schedule-template.ts getWeekendAdjustedDay keeps its own redundant `if (!rule.skipWeekend)` guard around the call. The helper stays coherent rather than drifting.
